newsitem.title: USA: Albright Middle East trip not imminent - Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Albright Middle East trip not imminent - Clinton.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Friday any visit by Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to the Middle East would only take place after an upcoming trip to the region by U.S. mediator Dennis Ross.

U.S. officials had said Albright was "weighing" a visit soon. But Clinton told reporters at the White House Ross would first make his trip, which had been due to start this week but was postponed to allow a period of mourning after Wednesday's Jerusalem bombing.

"When the period of mourning is over I will send Dennis Ross to the Middle East to meet with the leaders there with our latest ideas," Clinton said in answer to a question. "It was appropriate to delay that in view of the terrible loss of life and the bombing. Then we will see where we are," he added.

"I have said all along I will send the Secretary of State to the Middle East at the appropriate time. But i want Mr Ross to go there to do the work I am sending him there to do, to get the reaction of the leaders and then we will make a decision (on a trip by Albright)," he said.
Ross had been due to leave Washington on Wednesday for meetings with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
The trip was postponed after a double suicide bombing in a central Jerusalem market that killed the two bombers and 13 other people, interrupting tentative moves to restore stalled peace talks.
